questions.q: Explain the basis of Koeppen's classification of world climates.

answer.text: Koeppen's is the most widely used classification of world climates. It is an empirical system based on measurable data, chiefly the mean monthly and annual values of temperature and precipitation. Koeppen noticed that different climates support different natural vegetation, so he used vegetation as an indirect indicator of climate.

He grouped climates into five major types, marked by capital letters: A for tropical, B for dry, C for warm temperate, D for cold snow-forest, and E for polar. A separate group H denotes highland climates. Small letters are added to show the seasonal distribution and degree of temperature and rainfall, such as f for no dry season, w for dry winter and s for dry summer.
Thus Af stands for tropical rainforest, BW for desert, Cs for Mediterranean and ET for tundra.

answer: This scheme neatly links climate with temperature, rainfall and vegetation.
